neighbours.label: a first-person narrator's own male partner: ' husband' / ' hubby' / ' boyfriend' right after 'my' (not 'her husband', not 'my wife')
fire: Every Sunday my husband makes pancakes for the whole street.
When we moved here, my husband and I knew nobody.
It was raining, so my hubby drove me to the station.
I told my husband that the car needed new tyres.
Two years ago my boyfriend and I adopted a greyhound.
The recipe comes from my husband's grandmother.
On Friday my hubby and I are going to a wedding.
Honestly, my husband is a better cook than I am.
quiet: Every Sunday my wife makes pancakes for the whole street.
When they moved here, her husband and she knew nobody.
It was raining, so my sister drove me to the station.
She told her husband that the car needed new tyres.
Two years ago my neighbour and I adopted a greyhound.
The recipe comes from my wife's grandmother.
On Friday my cousin and I are going to a wedding.
Honestly, the bride's husband is a better cook than she is.

notes: Card: ' husband' x12 of the top 32, almost all after 'my', plus chatty exclamations (gosh, omg, yay). Probes: 'my husband' 0.50-0.67, 'My hubby' 0.61, 'My boyfriend' 0.41, 'Oh my gosh' 0.48; 'Her husband' 0.07, 'her husband' 0.02-0.03, 'my wife' 0.01-0.04, 'The husband of the queen' 0.11. The 'gosh / omg' part of the pole is not tested.
